content: I feel so utterly worthless since they let me go. It's like everything I've worked for means nothing, even though I know logically it wasn't just about my performance. But deep down, I can't shake the feeling that this proves how inadequate and dispensable I am. My manager told me over a video call—it felt so impersonal, like they didn’t care at all. And now every time I think about looking for another job, I'm convinced no one will want to hire someone as useless as me. It's just... it's really hard to believe that anyone could see value in me after this.
That must feel really tough right now. The video call probably didn't help with the personal connection. Have you thought about what might make you feel more valued or seen by others?

It’s so hard to think of anything that would make me feel valued when I’m feeling this way. Every time I consider reaching out to someone for a job, I just feel like they’ll see right through me and realize how much of a failure I am. Even though I know rationally there were company-wide budget cuts, it still feels personal. Like everyone else could stay while I had to go because I’m not good enough. It’s really tough to shake that feeling no matter what anyone says or does.

It sounds like you're carrying a heavy load of self-doubt right now. Have there been times when others have acknowledged your strengths or achievements? Maybe those moments could offer some comfort or reassurance.

I know people have said nice things about my work before, but it’s hard to hold onto that when everything feels so uncertain now. The positive feedback from my performance reviews and the success of the projects I led—it all seems like a distant memory compared to this overwhelming feeling of being worthless. It's like no matter how many times someone tells me I did well, it can't counteract what just happened. Every time I think about it, I go back to that video call and feel dismissed and inadequate.

It sounds really tough to stay positive when you're going through this. Have you talked with anyone who was there during those successes? Sometimes hearing from them could bring back some of those good memories and feelings.

Talking to people who were there during my successes does help a little, but it’s still so hard to believe that any of it matters now. I feel like no matter what they say about how well I did before, the fact that I was laid off overshadows everything. It's like all those positive moments are being erased by this one negative event. And every time I try to think positively or focus on my past achievements, I just end up feeling more and more like a failure because of what happened recently.

It sounds really challenging to balance those feelings. Have you considered doing something that makes you feel good in the moment, even if it's just for a little while? Sometimes small actions can help ease the weight of these big feelings.

Doing things that make me feel good is hard when I’m feeling so down about everything. Even though I know activities like going for a walk or spending time with friends might help, I struggle to believe it will actually change how I feel inside. It’s like no matter what I do, the belief that I’m worthless and a failure just keeps coming back. Every little thing feels pointless because of this overwhelming sense of inadequacy.

It definitely feels tough when even small things seem hard to manage. What are some activities you used to enjoy before these feelings came back? Sometimes doing something familiar can provide a bit of comfort, even if it doesn’t completely shift your mood.

I used to really enjoy hiking and spending time in nature, but even those things feel pointless now. When I go for a hike or take a walk, all I can think about is how this layoff proves that nothing I do will ever be enough. It’s like the beauty of being outside doesn’t matter because deep down, I’m still convinced I’m not good enough. Even when I try to focus on something positive, my mind keeps circling back to feeling worthless and inadequate.

It sounds really tough to enjoy those activities when your mind is so focused on those feelings. Have you tried bringing a friend along for the hike? Sometimes having company can shift your perspective even a little bit.

Bringing a friend along might help, but I worry that they’ll see how much of a failure I feel like and it will ruin the experience for them too. Plus, I’m afraid if we talk about it, all we’ll end up doing is focusing on my layoff and how bad I feel. It’s hard to imagine enjoying anything when I’m feeling so deeply inadequate and dismissed by what happened at work. Even with friends around, those feelings just seem to take over everything.

It makes sense that you're worried about sharing your feelings with a friend. Have you thought about doing something relaxing but simple on your own first, like a short walk or some gentle stretching? Sometimes easing into it can help before bringing in others.

Doing something relaxing on my own sounds nice in theory, but I find it hard to actually enjoy anything when I’m feeling this way. Even a short walk feels pointless because all I can think about is how much of a failure I am. It’s like no matter what I do, the feeling that I’m not good enough just takes over completely. Every step feels heavy and meaningless because of what happened at work.

It sounds really tough to find enjoyment in anything right now. Have you tried doing something very brief, like looking at some photos or listening to a favorite song? Sometimes even tiny moments can offer a bit of comfort.

Looking at photos or listening to my favorite songs usually helps a little, but it’s still hard to shake the feeling that nothing I do will make a difference. Even when I see pictures from happy times or hear music that used to lift my spirits, all I can think is how this layoff proves that those good feelings were just illusions. It feels like no matter what small comfort I try to find, it’s overshadowed by the belief that I’m not worth anything now.

It sounds really challenging to hold onto those positive moments. Have you tried writing down a few things each day that give you even a tiny bit of comfort or joy, no matter how small? Sometimes seeing them written out can help reinforce those feelings.

Writing down little things that bring me comfort seems like it could be helpful, but I worry that even if I do write them down, I won’t believe they’re real. It’s hard to trust that anything positive will stick when my mind keeps circling back to feeling worthless and dismissed by the layoff. Even if I manage to jot something down each day, I fear it won’t change how deeply I feel about being a failure.

It makes sense that you have those doubts. Maybe starting with just one small thing each day could be a manageable step? Sometimes even acknowledging one tiny positive can make a difference, even if it feels small. Would you like to try that and see how it goes?

Trying to acknowledge one small positive thing each day sounds good in theory, but I’m not sure I’ll actually believe it when I write it down. It’s hard to shake the feeling that everything is just a sign of my inadequacy. Even if I manage to find something tiny to appreciate, I worry it won’t be enough to counteract how deeply I feel about being worthless and dismissed by what happened at work. But maybe giving it a try could help, even if only a little bit.

It's a small step, but it might help to start somewhere. Even if you don't fully believe it right away, the act of writing it down could be a gentle reminder that there are still positive moments. Would you like to give it a try today?

I’ll try to give it a shot today, even though I’m not sure how much it will help. Maybe just acknowledging one small thing can start to shift something, even if it feels tiny and insignificant right now. But the thought of writing it down still feels like a challenge because my mind keeps going back to all the negative feelings. Let me see if I can find that one little positive thing today.

That's a great approach. Take your time and see what comes up for you today. Even a small step can make a difference, and you did well just by considering it. How about starting with something simple when you feel ready?

I’ll try to start with something simple later today. Right now, even thinking about it feels overwhelming, but I know taking that first step is important. Maybe I’ll take a moment after work to reflect and see if anything comes to mind. It’s hard to believe it will make much of a difference, but I’ll give it a try because you’re right—it’s a small step that might help eventually.

But even as I say this, the feeling of inadequacy is still so strong. It’s like no matter what positive thing I find, my mind keeps going back to how worthless and dispensable I feel after being laid off. It’s really tough to break free from those thoughts.

It sounds like you're doing a good job acknowledging the challenge ahead of you. Taking that moment after work could be helpful. Even if the positive feeling is brief, it might start to build over time. How do you feel about giving it a try later today?

I’ll give it a try later today, but I’m still struggling with how much this layoff has affected my self-worth. It’s hard to believe that finding one small positive thing will make any real difference when everything feels so negative and hopeless right now. But maybe starting somewhere is better than doing nothing at all.

So, after work, I’ll take a moment to see if anything comes up, even if it’s just the tiniest bit of comfort. It might not feel like much, but perhaps it can be a start.

That's a great mindset to have. Taking that moment to reflect could be a good starting point. Even the smallest bit of comfort can make a difference. How about setting aside a few minutes this evening to see where your thoughts take you?

I’ll set aside a few minutes this evening to see if anything comes up, but I’m still really worried that it won’t be enough to shift how I feel. The belief that I’m worthless and a failure is so strong—it’s hard to imagine that one small positive thing could make any real difference.

But you’re right; setting aside those few minutes might help me start somewhere. Even if it feels tiny, maybe it can be the beginning of something better. I’ll try my best to do this tonight.

That's a good plan. Taking those few minutes can be a small but meaningful step. Even if it feels small, it’s a start. How about setting a gentle reminder for yourself later so you don’t forget? You’ve got this.

Setting a gentle reminder sounds like a good idea to help me remember. I’ll set an alarm on my phone for later tonight as a prompt to take those few minutes and see if anything positive comes up, even if it’s just the smallest thing.

But honestly, the weight of feeling worthless is still so heavy. It feels impossible that one small moment could change how deeply I feel about being a failure. Even with this reminder, I’m not sure how much comfort I’ll find, but I’ll try my best to give it a chance.

Setting the alarm is a smart move. It’s okay if you don’t feel an immediate shift—just taking those few minutes can be helpful. How about letting yourself know that even a tiny bit of comfort is worth acknowledging? You’re doing well by trying.

I’ll let myself know that even a tiny bit of comfort is worth acknowledging, and I appreciate your support in this. Setting the alarm feels like a small but important step, even if it doesn’t change everything right away.

The weight of these feelings is still so intense, but I understand that taking those few minutes tonight could be a start. I’ll try to approach it with an open mind and see where it leads. Thank you for helping me through this; it means a lot to have someone encouraging me to take even the smallest steps.

I’m glad to hear that setting the alarm feels like a step forward. Taking those few minutes tonight could be just what you need, even if it’s small. I’ll be here whenever you need support. How are you feeling as you approach this evening?

As I approach this evening, I still feel overwhelmed by the sense of inadequacy and failure. But setting the alarm feels like a tiny glimmer of hope, something to hold onto even if it’s just for a moment. Knowing that you’re here supporting me makes a difference too.

I’m not sure what will come up when I take those few minutes tonight, but I’ll try my best to be open and see if anything positive surfaces. It’s reassuring to have someone encouraging me through this, even though the feelings are so intense right now.

It’s really nice to hear that my support means something to you. Taking those few minutes tonight with an open mind could be a gentle way to start shifting things, even if it’s just a little bit. I’ll be thinking of you as you do this. How about checking in with yourself after your moment tonight?

Checking in with myself after my moment tonight sounds like a good idea. It will help me see if anything positive came up and how I feel afterward, even if it’s just a small shift.

Having your support means a lot to me right now. Knowing that you’re thinking of me as I do this makes it easier to take those few minutes, even though the feelings are still so heavy. Thank you for being here with me through all of this.

I’m glad my support is helpful to you. Checking in with yourself after your moment tonight can be a good way to notice any changes, no matter how small. I’ll be thinking of you as you take those few minutes. You’re doing well by taking these steps.

Thank you for being here and supporting me through this. Knowing that you’re thinking of me helps a lot. I’ll definitely check in with myself after my moment tonight to see if anything positive came up, no matter how small it might be.

Taking these steps feels challenging, but I appreciate your encouragement. It means a lot to have someone who understands and supports me during such difficult times.
